title: Kernel fidelity validation suite and NVTX-to-SLO mapping
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Goal: Build a compact, reproducible validation suite and mapping layer that improves the fidelity of NVTX ranges and trace spans for kernel selection and prefill/decode scheduling. The suite must make it possible to reliably attribute tail latency and token-cost regressions to specific kernels, scheduling decisions, and attention optimizations while keeping runtime overhead low for production sampling.

Scope:
- Instrumentation conventions: canonical NVTX range names, stable span tags, and a minimal set of correlation keys (exec_id, stream_id, request_id, model_variant).
- A synthetic workload generator that exercises: varying sequence lengths, multi-stream interleaving, attention-cache hits/misses, and quantized vs fp16 kernels.
- A mapping/heuristic layer that aligns NVTX ranges to trace spans when CUDA stream reordering or asynchronous copies cause range fragmentation.
- Validation tests that measure mismatch rate between NVTX and span boundaries, kernel attribution accuracy, and the end-to-end latency attribution error under controlled conditions.
- Dashboards and alerts that surface integrity regressions (e.g., mismatch_rate > 3% for production sampling).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Low-overhead default: production will use sampled traces with coarse NVTX granularity (prefill_start/prefill_end, decode_start/decode_end, kernel_exec). Full per-kernel tagging is enabled only for debug builds or explicitly via feature flag. This balances observability and overhead.
- Heuristic alignment: when NVTX envelopes are split across streams, use monotonic GPU timestamps + host-side enqueue timestamps to compute best-fit alignments. Exact mapping is impossible in all cases; we provide a confidence score per attribution and surface low-confidence attributions in the UI for triage.
- Synthetic workload: prefer small, reproducible workloads that isolate single-kernel behaviors (e.g., single-attention-head stress tests) to avoid noisy attribution in multi-kernel overlapping traces.
- Backwards compatibility: agent supports older runtimes that only emit nvtx ranges by reconstructing spans from range metadata; when missing keys, tag as legacy and degrade to aggregate metrics.

Instrumentation plan:
1) Define a stable naming table for NVTX ranges and span tags; publish in the devdocs.
2) Add lightweight span wrappers in the scheduler hotpath that attach exec_id/stream_id.
3) Emit per-kernel metrics (duration_ms, tokens_processed, output_bytes, input_bytes, occupancy_pct) to the telemetry exporter with exec_id and cohort tags.
4) Implement an off-host mapping service (batch job) that reconciles NVTX envelopes with spans using monotonic timestamps and emits a reconciliation artifact for the dashboard.

Acceptance criteria:
- New canonical NVTX/span naming doc published and approved by Eng + Observability.
- Synthetic validation suite runs deterministically in CI with <1% variance for repeated runs.
- Mapping service reduces NVTX/span mismatch rate from baseline to <=3% on the validation corpus.
- Dashboards show per-model and per-kernel heatmaps; at least two alert rules firing on synthetic regression tests.
- Two internal PRs merged: runtime changes (lightweight tagging) and exporter changes (per-kernel metrics).

Rollout and risk mitigation:
- Feature-flag deploy: default off for low-latency prod clusters. Enable sampled tracing (1%) initially, then iterate.
- If mapping confidence is low for >5% of production traces, auto-disable expanded tagging and surface an incident for investigation.

Long-term: once stable, feed kernel attribution into the optimizer recommendation engine to suggest quantization or kernel switches for high-cost tokens.
